methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $17M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Hertha Metals is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $17M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine private robotics and manufacturing firms at similar or adjacent stages, supplemented by one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $17M raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement, implies a valuation of $34M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed)—yields a median of $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $1.8B. The wide disparity between methods reflects material uncertainty around whether Hertha should trade at a funding-round multiple (early-stage proxy) or a maturity-adjusted peer median (more developed stage companies).

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $29M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $842M. The low end reflects stage-based progression; the high end approaches peer medians. Key uncertainties include Hertha's operational maturity relative to Series B comparables, technology differentiation within the sector, and market traction relative to the named peer set. A more refined valuation would require clarity on revenue, unit economics, and competitive positioning versus the identified peer group.
